exposure: Birth anesthesia type (vaginal without anesthesia, vaginal with epidural anesthesia, cesarean section under subarachnoid block, cesarean section under general anesthesia)
outcome: Parameters of oxygenation and acid-base balance in umbilical cord blood (pH, hematocrit, total hemoglobin, blood oxygen capacity, carboxyhemoglobin content, hemoglobin oxygen saturation, oxygenated hemoglobin content, total oxygen content)
cohort: The study included mothers aged 18-45 and their newborns born from a singleton normal pregnancy lasting 37-42 weeks, with a birth weight between 2800 and 4100 g.
finding: The mean pH of umbilical cord arterial blood was significantly lowest (7.27) in the vaginal delivery with epidural anesthesia group, while oxygenation parameters were almost twice as high in cesarean sections under general anesthesia compared to regional anesthesia.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery with epidural anesthesia was associated with the lowest umbilical cord arterial blood pH, whereas general anesthesia during cesarean section led to significantly higher umbilical cord blood oxygenation parameters compared to regional anesthesia, regardless of delivery method.
